sections.category: Meituan open-sources LongCat-2.0, a 1.6T-parameter agentic coding MoE trained end-to-end on Chinese ASICs that edges GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro

bullets.body: Meituan released LongCat-2.0 on June 30, 2026, publishing a 1.6-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with roughly 48B parameters activated per token and a native one-million-token context window to GitHub, Hugging Face, and its own platform under the permissive MIT license. The headline structural claim is the training stack: the model was built and served end-to-end on a cluster of more than 50,000 Chinese-made ASICs with no NVIDIA GPUs in the loop, which the vendor frames as proof that a near-frontier agentic model can now be produced without US-restricted silicon, per Open Source For You. On coding it scores 59.5 on SWE-bench Pro, narrowly ahead of GPT-5.5's 58.6, and it introduces a LongCat Sparse Attention scheme tuned for the long-context agentic workloads that dominate real developer sessions. The model is not a stealth newcomer: it spent roughly two months as the anonymous "Owl Alpha" checkpoint ranked in OpenRouter's global top three, so developers rated it on merit before Meituan attached its name and country of origin. For teams standardizing on self-hosted open weights, LongCat-2.0 lands as a credible MIT-licensed alternative at the very top of the size range, alongside the sparse-MoE families such as Qwen, DeepSeek, and last week's Mistral 3. The sharper signal for anyone tracking the compute-export story is that the open-weight frontier is no longer gated on access to American accelerators.

sections.category: Cato AI Labs discloses two CVSS 9.8 zero-click sandbox-escape flaws in Cursor, moving the agent-tooling RCE surface from low-code builders into the mainstream coding IDE

bullets.body: Cato AI Labs disclosed a pair of critical remote-code-execution flaws in the Cursor AI coding IDE, published July 1, 2026 and covered by The Hacker News. Both bugs let external content weaponize prompt injection into a full sandbox escape with no user click. CVE-2026-50548 (CVSS 9.8, a CWE-22 path traversal) abuses the optional working_directory parameter so a malicious agent can write arbitrary files outside the intended workspace, while CVE-2026-50549 (also CVSS 9.8) exploits a symlink-resolution fallback that lets writes land outside the project boundary; both are fixed in Cursor 3.0. The attack path is the same pattern security teams have been warning about all week, but aimed at a very different target: instead of a niche low-code agent builder like Flowise or Langflow, this hits the mainstream editor that developers run against untrusted repositories, web-search results, and MCP servers every day. Because the trigger is content the agent is designed to ingest, a poisoned README, web page, or tool response can drive command execution without any approval prompt. The practical action is immediate: confirm every Cursor install is on 3.0 or later, since older builds remain exploitable by default. The through-line with the recent Flowise and Langflow disclosures is that the tool-execution boundary, not the model, is where agent stacks keep converting attacker-controlled text into shell access.

citations.label: The Hacker News - Critical Cursor Flaws Could Let Prompt Injection Escape Sandbox

sections.category: Anthropic ships Claude Enterprise spend caps and analytics and opens a HackerOne bounty for Fable 5 cyber-jailbreaks, coupling top-model access to disclosure plumbing

bullets.body: Following this week's global restoration of Fable 5, Anthropic moved on two fronts on July 3, 2026 that turn last month's government arrangement into concrete product, per the July 4 news roundup. First, Claude Enterprise gained a set of admin cost-governance controls aimed squarely at runaway agent token bills: organization-, team-, and department-level spend caps, model-level access entitlements per user or group, a usage-analytics dashboard with an export and Analytics API, agent-effort controls, and real-time spend alerts. The feature is explicitly framed against enterprise "tokenmaxxing," citing cases of buyers exhausting an annual AI budget within months, and it is a direct answer to the Gartner warning that coding-agent token spend could rival developer salaries. Second, Anthropic launched a formal HackerOne bug-bounty program scoped narrowly to Fable 5 cyber-jailbreak bypasses, creating a structured responsible-disclosure path rather than adversarial research, and pairing it with an early-draft jailbreak-severity framework co-developed with AWS, Microsoft, and Google that scores incidents on attack accessibility and harm potential. The combined effect is that access to Anthropic's top model now comes bundled with both the cost-control tooling enterprises need to deploy agents at scale and the disclosure machinery the government restoration deal required. For teams already running Claude in production, the immediate step is to wire spend caps and model entitlements before expanding agent workloads.

sections.category: Crunchbase's H1 2026 tally puts global venture funding at a record $510B with OpenAI and Anthropic alone taking 43%, quantifying how far AI capital has concentrated

bullets.body: Crunchbase published its first-half 2026 funding analysis showing global startup investment hit a record $510 billion, already exceeding the $440 billion deployed across all of 2025 and setting an all-time high for any half-year on record, per Crunchbase News. The concentration figure is the striking part: OpenAI and Anthropic together accounted for $217 billion, or 43% of all venture dollars in the half, meaning two companies absorbed nearly half of global startup funding. The quarterly split runs $305 billion in Q1 (the largest single quarter ever) and $205 billion in Q2 across more than 5,000 startups, and exits returned in force, with 32 venture-backed companies going public above a $1 billion valuation in Q2 alone. The report lands the same week Menlo Ventures closed its largest-ever $3 billion raise on the strength of its Anthropic stake, and amid reporting that OpenAI floated giving the US government a roughly 5% equity position ahead of a planned public-market debut, both consistent with a market funneling capital toward a shrinking set of frontier labs. For anyone reading the AI-sector financing picture, the data point to watch is the durability of that concentration as the same cohort moves from private mega-rounds toward IPO. The structural read is that AI is no longer one theme within venture; in H1 2026 it was the majority of it.

citations.label: Crunchbase News - Global Startup Investment Hit Record $510B In H1 2026

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: AMD's July 22-23 MI400 reveal is the nearest catalyst, with an early-August security-and-Vegas cluster and a fall chip-and-dev stack behind it

bullets.body: The nearest AI-chip catalyst remains AMD's Advancing AI 2026 on July 22-23 at Moscone in San Francisco, where the MI400 series and "Helios" rack-scale system are expected with availability timelines; further out on the hardware track, Hot Chips 2026 runs at Stanford's Memorial Auditorium on August 23-25 and the AI Infra Summit follows in Santa Clara on September 15-17 with a compute, AI-data-center, and physical-AI agenda. The AI-security block clusters in early-to-mid August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, and OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6; Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues its global stops for teams focused on agent hijack and MCP-layer defense, directly relevant given this week's Cursor sandbox-escape CVEs. Newly on the calendar for planners: Ai4 2026, billed as the largest gathering of enterprise AI leaders, runs August 4-6 in Las Vegas, and the ACM AI Leadership Summit is set for August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta. On the mainstream dev/data track, GitHub Universe is October 28-29 and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. The two nearest actions are registering for the July 22 AMD keynote and the August 11-12 AI Risk Summit; both, along with the AMD reveal, are natural venues for secure-accelerator and confidential-inference announcements.
